title: add-jsonschema-strict-mode-enhanced-errors-openai-compat
author: Ava Chen
description:
Background: We already support response_format=json_schema in the API but customers have reported confusing error messages and inconsistent behavior in strict mode (the API option that enforces schema conformance and rejects/terminates streaming on invalid output). This PR improves validation error messages, tightens strict-mode semantics for streaming clients, and extends the OpenAI-compatibility layer so users calling via the /v1/ completions/chat endpoints get the same behavior.

What this PR does: - Introduces structured validation error payloads with detailed path, validator, and sample failing token context when response_format.strict=true. Errors are returned in a single-line JSON metadata field for non-streaming responses and emitted as a final validation event for streaming responses. - Changes streaming behavior in strict mode: the server now sends an explicit "validation_error" stream event with the structured error and then closes the stream with a clear termination reason (previously streams would close with an ambiguous error). Clients can opt into graceful fallback by setting response_format.strict=false or setting response_format.fallback_to_text=true. - Adds OpenAI compatibility mappings: the legacy openai-compat wrapper now accepts response_format: {type: "json_schema", strict: true} and maps it consistently to the internal response_format fields. It also translates validation events to an equivalent OpenAI-style "error" event so tooling and SDKs see a consistent surface. - Improves server-side schema validator to include: (1) pointer to JSON path (RFC6901 style), (2) failing schema keyword, (3) an example token-level context (up to ~160 chars) to help debugging streaming truncation issues, and (4) suggestion hints when a missing required field can be inferred from prompts (heuristic). - Adds unit & integration tests covering strict streaming termination, event ordering, and backwards compatibility with non-strict / legacy clients.

Motivation: Better developer experience for customers building structured-output guarantees (eg. ingestion pipelines, downstream validation). Previously reported support tickets indicated ambiguous errors and many user-side retries; clarifying the error semantics will reduce support load and improve platform reliability.

Checklist: - [x] Add structured validation error schema and marshaling - [x] Implement streaming validation event + termination reason - [x] Map compatibility layer and SDK surface changes - [x] Add unit and integration tests - [x] Documentation for response_format.strict and fallback behavior - [x] Changelog entry and release notes

Compatibility: Non-strict mode behavior is unchanged. OpenAI-compat clients will see the new structured error event but only when they opt into strict mode via response_format.strict or the equivalent compat mapping. Fallback behavior is opt-in to avoid surprising existing callers.
